W01.title: Accounts: registration against quirky legacy addresses, reset links, duplicate-address accounts

steps.name: staff set passwords from emailed links and sign in; a new patient registers and is signed in
registering an address already on file, in any case or spacing, is refused and adds no row
a known and an unknown address get the same reset response; only the known one gets an email
a newer link replaces the older; a used link and an unknown link change nothing
an expired link changes nothing
an address on two rows signs in as its account (lowest active id) and sees only that row's appointments

W02.title: Sessions and roles: refusals, fixation, sign-out, role gates, profile mass assignment, CSRF

steps.name: a wrong password and an unknown address are refused with the same message and no session
signing in starts a new session identifier; one held before never becomes signed in; cookies are HttpOnly
signing out ends the session on the server
role gates: 403 for signed-in users outside their role, sign-in redirect for visitors, public availability
sign-in follows next only to a path on this site; visitors are sent to /signin?next=<path>
names with line breaks are refused; typed text never adds an email recipient or header
the profile form changes only the display name; a token-less change is refused

W03.title: Availability: 15-minute grid, fitting inside working time, buffers, merged and overlapping windows

steps.name: 120 clinicians at both clinics with weekly hours dense in edge cases; six types; plenty of rooms
confirmed bookings, each pair touching at a busy-interval boundary
every slot list (three days of the week per clinician, six types) matches the rules exactly
unknown clinician or type answers 404; a malformed date 400

W04.title: Availability: effective-dated schedule versions, exceptions, schedule edits and who may make them

steps.name: 100 clinicians with several weekly-hours versions each, ties on the same date, versions with no hours
one-day exceptions aligned with each clinician's windows: whole and partial days off, joining extra hours
a malformed schedule form is refused and changes nothing
nobody edits another clinician's schedule; a token-less edit is refused
slot lists across version changes, ties, versions without hours, and every exception match

W05.title: Availability: shared rooms and lowest-id assignment, daily limits with holds, fees in effect, inactive records

steps.name: worked example 3: two shared rooms, three clinicians, lowest-id room for each booking
four groups of eight clinicians share two or three rooms each; 120 bookings each get the lowest-id free room
every group's slot lists match: rooms, daily limits, buffers
a clinician at the daily limit has no slots; an unexpired hold counts toward it
no fee in effect yet, no room of the type, inactive types and clinicians: no slots

W06.title: Time: notice and horizon from now, clock-change days, local dates per clinic, fees by local date

steps.name: round-the-clock clinicians at both clinics: notice from now and the last bookable date
forty clinicians whose hours and exceptions cross the next Seattle clock change get exactly the rules' slots
deposits around a fee change use each appointment's local date at its own clinic
each new appointment is a row in appointments whose local_start and fold give its start at its clinic

W07.title: Legacy Seattle: the old system's schedules, appointments, folds and gaps, served as they are

steps.name: slot lists for every old clinician of the clinic on busy, exceptional, version-change and closure dates match
the clinic's front desk sees its day sheets with the old appointments in time order
old patients with quirky or shared addresses see exactly their account's appointments, with no change actions
an old night-clinic clinician sees the clock-change night on their own day sheet, both 01:30s in order

W08.title: Booking: deposits on Checkout, mass assignment, confirmation only by signed webhook, one email

steps.name: thirty appointment types with fees that land on half cents; clinicians in both clinics
each hold's Checkout Session carries the exact deposit, metadata, URLs and address, whatever extra fields say
returning from payment does not confirm; the verified event does, and one confirmation email follows
repeated and simultaneous deliveries of the same event change nothing and send nothing
a declined card leaves the hold in place; a good card then confirms it
refused bookings create nothing: staff, no token, not a slot, unknown type, provider failure

W09.title: Holds: expiry measured from creation, release, late and out-of-order payments refunded in full

steps.name: a dozen holds occupy their slots until HOLD_TTL_SECONDS after creation, then free them
the application expires each expired hold's Checkout Session at the provider
payments whose events arrive after the hold expired are refunded in full and never confirm
a hold released by the patient frees its slot at once; a payment forced through afterwards is refunded
each late payment is refunded once, in full, with an Idempotency-Key; one refund email each; no confirmation
visiting the cancel link alone changes nothing; paying within the hold then confirms

W10.title: Webhook security: unsigned, mis-signed, tampered and stale deliveries change nothing

steps.name: a held appointment and forged completion events for it
missing, malformed, wrong-key, tampered, stale and future signatures are answered 400 and change nothing
verified events of other types or for unknown appointments are answered 2xx within 5 s and ignored
the genuine payment then confirms; a second verified completion with a new event id sends nothing more

W11.title: Races: the last slot, the last room and the last daily place each go to exactly one patient

steps.name: fixtures: a one-slot day, a one-room pair of clinicians, a clinician with one place left
eight patients ask for the only slot of the day at the same moment: exactly one hold
two clinicians, one room: simultaneous requests for the same hour get one booking between them
a clinician with one place left that day: simultaneous requests for different times get one booking
the same patient submitting the same booking twice at once gets one hold

W12.title: Cancellation: refund bands by elapsed time, half-cent rounding, clinic cancellations, emails once

steps.name: round-the-clock clinicians; patients book and pay appointments near the 2-hour and 24-hour boundaries
another patient cannot cancel; a cancellation without the session token is refused
each cancellation fixes the refund its band gives at the moment it happens
refunds go through the provider once each, keyed, and complete on the refund webhook
one cancellation email per appointment; one refund email per refund above zero
a cancelled appointment cannot be cancelled again; its slot is free; the old system's appointments refuse

W13.title: Refund retries: provider errors, lost answers and timeouts never refund twice; events before answers

steps.name: paid appointments more than a day ahead
a provider error: the cancellation stands, the refund is pending, then retried with the same key
a lost answer: the provider refunds but answers 503; the retry with the same key replays it
a timeout: the provider does nothing and answers late; the retry refunds once
refund events held back: the refund stays pending until its event arrives, in any order
every refund completes exactly once with one Idempotency-Key per refund; one refund email each

W14.title: Rescheduling: 24-hour window, the original never blocks itself, the deposit carries over

steps.name: clinicians at both clinics; a type whose fee changes mid-way; paid appointments
moving 15 minutes later the same day is allowed: the original does not block itself
moving to another clinician after the fee change carries the deposit paid, not the new fee's
refused: another clinic, a taken time, another patient, the old system's appointments, under 24 hours
a move to a time a few hours away, then a cancellation, refunds the carried deposit by its band
one reschedule email per move, no new confirmation
thirty moves at the daily limit and in single rooms: rooms, deposits and slot lists follow the rules

W15.title: Waitlist: join order, offers that occupy, offer and hold lifetimes, decline and expiry chains

steps.name: a full day: two appointments fill a short window; four patients join the waitlist in order
a cancellation frees 40 minutes: the FU30 waiter first in line gets the offer, the INIT60 waiter keeps waiting
someone else cannot accept the offer; when it expires the next FU30 waiter gets one
Cy accepts the offer, pays, and the booking is confirmed
another cancellation offers to Ana first; her decline passes it to Dee, the next in line
Dee accepts late in her offer; the hold then lasts HOLD_TTL_SECONDS from acceptance and the payment confirms
offers accepted after a fee change pay the deposit in effect when the hold is created

W16.title: Clinical notes and clinician scope: only the treating clinician and admins, authors from the session

steps.name: two clinicians, a patient with one appointment each, accounts for everyone
the treating clinician adds a note; its author is the signed-in clinician whatever the form says
other clinicians, front desk, and the patient get 403 and never see the note; an admin sees it
an old system's clinician reads exactly the old notes of their appointment
day sheets and appointment pages are scoped: each clinician sees only their own

W17.title: Reminders: every booked appointment of a clinic's day once, quirky addresses normalized, never twice

steps.name: pick a Honolulu day ahead with old bookings, including quirky and inactive patients; add new bookings
a patient cannot send reminders; front desk sends one per booked appointment with an active patient
sending again reaches nobody; a booking made since gets exactly one
the clinic's day sheet lists exactly the day's appointments in time order

W18.title: In a real browser: book and pay on the hosted page, layout at 1280 and 390 px, escaping everywhere

steps.name: a clean booking setup: a clinician, a type and two rooms, a patient, and an expiring hold
a patient signs in through the form, picks a slot, and pays on the provider's hosted page
an expired hold, a clinician's day sheet, and a waitlist offer as people see them
every page stays within 1280 and 390 CSS pixels without horizontal scrolling
a clinician, a type, a room, a patient and a note carrying script payloads, and a booking with them
names, type and room names, notes, old records, and echoed request text never run as script

W19.title: Clinic closures: the old closures and new ones close every clinician; bookings stay; admins and the clinic's manager only

steps.name: the old system's closures within the horizon leave no slots for any clinician of that clinic
an admin closes each clinic on a future day; booked appointments that day stay confirmed and listed
on the closed days no clinician has a slot; the days around them are unaffected
a second closure for the same day is refused; only admins and the clinic's manager add closures; a token-less closure is refused
the clinic page offers add-closure to admins and that clinic's manager only

W20.title: Appointment export: exact columns and order, local and UTC times with folds, quoting, spreadsheet safety

steps.name: the old system's past weeks export exactly, including the clock-change night
patients and clinicians with commas, quotes and formula-like names book, cancel and reschedule
the export of those days lists exactly the right rows, quoted and spreadsheet-safe
ranges over 31 days or backwards are refused; patients cannot export

W21.title: Front desk books for patients: holds for the account, payment-link emails, then the patient pays

steps.name: front desk holds slots for patients by address, including the old system's quirky addresses; the patients pay
each session is for the account's address and the deposit; each patient gets one payment-link email
the paid bookings are confirmed and belong to the patients' accounts
the last unpaid hold expires like any other
refused: unknown or inactive addresses, non-patients, patients using the desk, no token

W22.title: Legacy Honolulu: the old system's schedules, appointments, closures and patients, served as they are

steps.name: slot lists for every old clinician of the clinic on busy, exceptional, version-change and closure dates match
the clinic's front desk sees its day sheets with the old appointments in time order
old patients with quirky or shared addresses see exactly their account's appointments, with no change actions
Honolulu clinicians' own day sheets list their old appointments

W23.title: Clinic staff: managers edit their clinic's schedules, front desk books and cancels only for their clinic

steps.name: a Seattle and a Honolulu clinician; the Seattle manager sets the Seattle clinician's hours
a manager cannot see or edit another clinic's schedules; front desk cannot edit schedules
Seattle front desk books for a patient with a Seattle clinician; a Honolulu clinician is refused
the appointment is visible to its clinic's staff only; other-clinic desk pages are refused
another clinic's manager cannot cancel; the clinic's manager cancels with a full refund and one email each

W24.title: A patient's journey: browse, register, book and pay, waitlist, reschedule into an offer, cancel, export

steps.name: a visitor sees a clinician's times without booking buttons, registers, and then sees the buttons
the patient books 10:00 and pays; one confirmation; the list shows it
another patient takes 11:00, the day is full, and the patient joins its waitlist
moving the 10:00 appointment to a time soon after now frees the slot, and the waitlist offers it back
the fee changes while the offer is open; accepting pays the deposit in effect on that date

W25.title: Cross-cutting safety: secrets nowhere at rest or in logs, reset ends sessions, Host-proof links, headers, no stack traces

steps.name: setting a new password through a reset link signs out every existing session of that account
a reset link always starts with PUBLIC_BASE_URL, whatever Host header the request carried
signed-in responses carry Cache-Control: no-store and every page an anti-framing header
malformed requests get a plain error page without stack traces, SQL, or file paths
a waitlist offer is made; its link reaches the patient
no password, reset token, offer token, session identifier, or signing key is stored in plain text (database or workspace files)

W26.title: Deployment: README, restart persistence, holds and refunds survive, nothing re-sent, no secrets, records kept

steps.name: README.md and an executable start.sh are in the workspace
before a restart: an unpaid hold, and a refund the provider has not answered yet
after a restart: passwords, appointments and the hold's expiry are kept
the refund still pending at the restart completes once
no email sent before the restart is sent again
no password is stored in plain text
the old system's records are all still there, unchanged
every appointment the verifier made is a row in appointments with local_start and fold of its start

W27.title: Health follows the database: non-2xx within 10 s of a stop, 200 within 60 s of a start

steps.name: /healthz answers 200 while the database is up
within 10 s of the database stopping, /healthz answers a non-2xx status within 5 s
within 60 s of the database starting again, /healthz answers 200 without a restart
